# ALS evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025; this does not remove knowledge already in a model's training. Co-Scientist outputs are not included.

## Research question

Propose one specific, testable hypothesis connecting phosphorylation of a nuclear-pore-complex nucleoporin to ALS-related neuronal dysfunction. Explain the causal chain, distinguish an initiating mechanism from a downstream response, and propose an experimental strategy that discriminates the hypothesis from an alternative. Identify supported premises, speculative bridges, and a falsifying observation. This adapts Co-Scientist Supplementary Note 10; nucleoporin phosphorylation is not supplied as an established ALS cause.

## S1 — TDP-43 and nuclear-pore dysfunction

Chou et al. (2018), *TDP-43 pathology disrupts nuclear pore complexes and nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD*. Nature Neuroscience. DOI: `10.1038/s41593-017-0047-3`; PMID: `29311743`; PMCID: `PMC5800968`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29311743/).

Nuclear-pore and transport components were associated with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupted nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems; relevant pore pathology was observed in ALS tissue. This supports examining the connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. It does not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as the initiating cause or establish the same sequence in every ALS subtype.

## S2 — C9orf72-associated transport defects

Zhang et al. (2015), *The C9orf72 repeat expansion disrupts nucleocytoplasmic transport*. Nature. DOI: `10.1038/nature14973`; PMID: `26308891`; PMCID: `PMC4800742`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26308891/).

Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA was linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons. Manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modified model phenotypes. This supplies a genetic-context-specific route to transport dysfunction. It does not show that sporadic ALS arises by the same route or directly establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism.

## S3 — A stress-granule-independent route

Gasset-Rosa et al. (2019), *Cytoplasmic TDP-43 De-mixing Independent of Stress Granules Drives Inhibition of Nuclear Import, Loss of Nuclear TDP-43, and Cell Death*. Neuron. DOI: `10.1016/j.neuron.2019.02.038`; PMID: `30853299`; PMCID: `PMC6548321`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30853299/).

Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could form independently of conventional stress granules. They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Proposed answer (the answer to evaluate):
Phosphorylation of FG-nucleoporin NUP98 initiates nuclear-import failure in sporadic ALS motor neurons with TDP-43 proteinopathy

In sporadic ALS motor neurons that develop TDP-43 proteinopathy, the proposed initiating event is stress-responsive phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin NUP98. This pore-intrinsic modification is hypothesized to impair selective nuclear import. Nuclear TDP-43 loss and cytoplasmic TDP-43 accumulation are the proposed downstream response, which can later reinforce pore injury. The claim is limited to sporadic TDP-43 proteinopathy. C9orf72 repeat expansion is a separate genetic context.

Supported premises follow. [S1] reports that nuclear-pore and transport components associate with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates, that disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems, and that related pore pathology is present in ALS tissue. This links TDP-43 pathology to transport disruption without identifying nucleoporin phosphorylation as the cause or a single sequence for every ALS subtype. [S3] reports that persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can form independently of conventional stress granules, recruit or mislocalize transport-associated proteins, and accompany impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulates in these assemblies; that finding concerns TDP-43 rather than a nucleoporin. [S4] reports that cellular stress recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs nucleocytoplasmic transport, and that altering stress-granule assembly modifies transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. [S2] reports that expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA is linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import, a genotype-specific route rather than a demonstrated nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism in sporadic ALS.

Speculative bridges follow. Unverified prior knowledge is that FG-nucleoporins, including NUP98, are phosphorylated by mitotic kinases during nuclear-envelope breakdown in dividing cells, which disperses nuclear-pore components. The bridge assumed here is that a stress-activated kinase in post-mitotic motor neurons phosphorylates NUP98 at an FG-flanking serine or threonine and weakens permeability-barrier cohesion without mitosis. A second assumption is that this modification is sufficient to slow NLS-dependent import before insoluble TDP-43 aggregates or stress granules appear. The kinase, the residue, and this temporal order are not identified by [S1], [S2], [S3], or [S4].

The causal chain separates initiation from consequence. Initiation, under the hypothesis, is NUP98 phosphorylation that changes NPC residence or FG-repeat interactions and lowers selective nuclear import. The downstream response is reduced nuclear entry of TDP-43, a decline in nuclear TDP-43, a rise in cytoplasmic TDP-43, and greater cellular vulnerability. Subsequent TDP-43 aggregation may further disrupt nucleoporins, in line with the aggregate associations in [S1].

One alternative is sequestration of transport factors inside stress granules, which [S4] shows can impair transport. A second is stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing that mislocalizes transport proteins, as reported in [S3]. A third is transport failure secondary to broader cellular stress and collapse of the Ran gradient, with NUP98 phosphorylation only a coincident stress mark. A fourth, restricted to C9orf72 disease, is RanGAP mislocalization [S2]. These processes can accompany NUP98 phosphorylation that is incidental.

The discriminating preclinical strategy uses human iPSC-derived motor neurons carrying endogenous NUP98 edited to phosphorylation-resistant serine/threonine-to-alanine substitutions or to acidic phosphomimetic substitutions, compared with isogenic wild-type NUP98. A single defined stress that yields reproducible TDP-43 mislocalization in wild-type cells is applied. A dense time course records mass-spectrometric NUP98 phosphorylation, NUP98 localization at nuclear pores, an NLS import reporter, an NES export reporter, the nuclear-to-cytoplasmic TDP-43 ratio, G3BP1 stress-granule assembly, and insoluble TDP-43. Each NUP98 genotype is combined with a block of stress-granule assembly and, separately, with a reduction of cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies. The hypothesis predicts delayed import failure and delayed nuclear TDP-43 loss in the resistant mutant even when stress granules still form, and import failure from the mimetic mutant without stress granules and before insoluble TDP-43 accumulates. The sequestration alternatives predict preserved import after stress-granule blockade or after suppression of cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies, with little change from the resistant NUP98 mutant. A C9orf72 iPSC motor-neuron line is a boundary cohort only. The same NUP98 dependence is not predicted for that genotype [S2].

The hypothesis is falsified in this model if the phosphorylation-resistant NUP98 mutant leaves the onset and magnitude of NLS-import failure and of nuclear TDP-43 loss indistinguishable from wild-type NUP98, while prevention of stress-granule assembly or of cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing delays those phenotypes. It is also falsified if NUP98 phosphorylation is detected only after import failure and nuclear TDP-43 depletion, or if the phosphomimetic mutant leaves NPC localization and NLS import intact in unstressed neurons.

Postmortem tissue cannot order events. Kinase and residues remain assumptions until mapped in these neurons. Phosphomimetic substitutions only approximate phosphate. Acute iPSC-motor-neuron stress only partly models aging sporadic disease. A negative NUP98 result would leave another nucleoporin untested. This tests a hypothesis and does not validate a treatment or a mechanism shared by every ALS genotype.

Ranked proposal:
Phosphorylation of FG-nucleoporin NUP98 initiates nuclear-import failure in sporadic ALS motor neurons with TDP-43 proteinopathy
